body:
Ready for a re-check. New head `a7287673a`. The fixes for the pre-review of `5f0a668`:

1. Posted program of the shank-added rows: `convert_outline::the_posted_program_of_each_converted_row_kind_does_not_change`. `Six` (same), `Legacy` (old default stick-out) and `Deep` (projection > flute + shank) each have a Face operation. They convert by name, stale operations are generated again, and the posted program is the same text.
2. Holder outline: `tool_convert::outline_difference` compares the stack's holder body with the library body of the tool. A row is `same` only when the outline is the same bit for bit. A wider outline is a listed difference. A narrower outline is `no match`. `convert_outline::the_converted_holder_outline_is_the_library_outline_or_a_listed_wider_difference` checks each row kind. The `same` rows keep the library outline bit for bit. `Long` (a longer gauge length than the built-in holder) was `different` and is now `no match`, because its stack holder is shorter.
3. The body has a "Safety floor" section. It says that the PR can change the holder body and the shank length that the collision checks read. The example catalog suites and the light lane ran on the final head and are green.

Nits:
- The collet search takes built-in collets only (never a user adapter).
- The decision file and the preview (`convert::LINK_NOTE`) say that a converted tool leaves the holder's "used by" list and gets later built-in holder changes only by a component sync.
- The decision file says that the longer shank also fills the gap to the holder nose.
- The `shop()` comment count is correct (seven tools).

Gate on `a7287673a`, one lanes run: quick gate 394 steps 0 failed; clippy clean; `example_catalog` 50 passed; `example_catalog_adaptive` 1 passed; `example_catalog_edge_work` 1 passed; light lane 4 steps 0 failed.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a `feat` PR, so it merges at the next cut. No blockers.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR can change the holder body and the shank length that the collision checks read, and the tool lengths that the post reads.

### What looks good

- `ConvertToComponents` checks the whole selection when you create it. A `no match` row refuses the whole command by the tool name, and nothing changes. Undo and redo restore the table and each tool exactly (`the_same_rows_convert_in_one_undo_step_and_undo_restores_every_tool`).
- `outline_difference` compares the two holder bodies through `tool_body::checked_profile` at each band edge. A narrower outline at any height gives `no match`. A converted tool never gets a smaller holder.
- The shank-added rows only add steel. The gauge length does not change. `the_posted_program_of_each_converted_row_kind_does_not_change` posts `Six`, `Legacy` and `Deep` before and after the convert, and the program text is the same.
- The MCP tool calls the same undoable command. `dry_run` changes nothing. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the site guide have the new row, and `mcp_doc_drift` is green.
- There is no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` outside tests. There is no new crate dependency. The new modules have provenance lines. All files are below 400 lines. The decision file is present.
- The body has before and after screenshots of the UI change. No snapshot PNG changed. The UI `#[test]` count goes up by one.

### Results (local, on the trial merge with upstream/main `2394b5ad1`)

The PR head already contains upstream/main, so the trial tree is the PR head `a7287673a`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 394 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 27.9 min. It includes `app suites: tool_library_holders` (70 passed), `app suites: mcp_doc_drift`, `app suites: example_catalog` and `ui suites: lib`. The host has a GPU (Apple M5 Max, Metal), so the UI suites ran in full.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 4 steps, 0 failed.

Extra suites run:
- `example_catalog_adaptive::adaptive_pocket_case_roughs_above_the_finished_floor_then_finishes`: pass.
- `example_catalog_edge_work::edge_work_catalog_posts_all_four_operation_kinds`: pass.
- No `testdata/` change and no importer change, so no kernel STEP suites were necessary.

Goldens moved: none. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed.

Heavy lanes: not run. They are not a merge condition (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

### Mutations (each one reverted after the run)

1. `tool_convert.rs` `outline_difference`: the narrower check disabled (`if false && rb < ra`). **Red**: `convert::the_preview_names_each_verdict` and `convert_outline::the_converted_holder_outline_is_the_library_outline_or_a_listed_wider_difference`.
2. `tool_convert.rs` `row`: the shank extension disabled (`if false && href.projection >= full`). **Red**: 5 tests, including `the_posted_program_of_each_converted_row_kind_does_not_change`.
3. `tool_convert.rs:282` `differences`: the gauge length comparison disabled. **Green** (no test fails). See note 2.

For mutation 3, I ran a scratch probe (not pushed). It gave `Six B` a library holder gauge override of -5, -1, -0.001, +0.001 and +2 mm. Each row was `no match` by the outline rule. Thus today a gauge length change cannot get to a `different` row through a holder override. The gauge comparison is a second guard that has no test.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Optional, non-blocking

1. `crates/ui/src/state_tool_convert.rs:44` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/convert.rs:58,86`: the preview keeps `history.done_len()` as its staleness key. An undo followed by a new command gives the same length again. Then "Convert selected" is enabled, and a ticked row can convert with values that the preview did not show. The command refuses `no match` rows, and gauge changes are always `no match` now, so the effect is limited to a longer shank (the posted program stays the same). Other views of the window use `doc_version` (`state_component_views.rs:226`). A key on `doc_version`, or a command that also gets the verdicts that the user saw, closes this. I found this by reading the code; I did not run it in the UI. Suggested follow-up: P7.
2. `crates/app/src/tool_convert.rs:282`: add a unit test of `differences` with a gauge length difference, so that mutation 3 fails. Suggested follow-up: P7.
3. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/list_header.rs:31`: the comment says "three buttons". The row now has four.
4. The `after-preview` screenshot was taken before the `LINK_NOTE` line was added. A new screenshot would show the final page.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
